what_it_is: The calls of an association study that Python and TypeScript both
refuse, the values that neither refuses because both read them as a
number, the values that mean no phenotype in both, and the two that
TypeScript alone refuses. It is the one file
of this directory that no reference program wrote: the others are what
plink2, GMMAT and rrBLUP answered, and this is a list the two test
suites read so that neither layer can refuse something the other
accepts without this file saying that it does.
`case` is the call, which each suite writes in its own language over
the worked example of `docs/specs/gwas.md`; a case that a suite has no
call for fails that suite, which is what makes the file bind. `match`
is a regular expression that the message of both layers has to hold, so
it is written out of the words the two share and not out of one of
them: the names of the arguments differ between the two languages, and
so does the quoting of a name in a message.
`refusals` are the calls both layers refuse. Each of them is a
`ValueError` in Python unless the case says otherwise in
`python_raises`, which is `TypeError` where what the user wrote is of
the wrong type altogether; JavaScript has one `Error` for all of them.
A case whose refusal comes from the machinery of its own language, and
not from words popnei wrote, has `match_in_python` and
`match_in_typescript` in place of `match`: what binds there is that
both layers refuse the call, since neither message can hold the
other's words.
`coercions` are the calls where a value that is not a number reaches
the study as one: each of them is the worked example written another
way, so each suite asserts the null model that example gives and no
case there has a `match`.
`no_phenotype_in_both_layers` are the values that mean an individual
with no phenotype, which is left untested rather than refused. The rule
the spec settled on 23 September 2026 is by the oracle: a value means
no phenotype exactly where Python's `float` of it gives NaN, which NaN
itself and the string `nan` both do. Each suite asserts a study of the
five individuals that `i2` is not among.
`refused_in_typescript_alone` is the divergence that is left. Python
says that an individual has no phenotype with a name the series has
not, with `None` and with the missing value of pandas, which `dropna`
drops; TypeScript has neither, and `float(None)` raises, so `null` and
`undefined` are refused there. Each suite asserts its own half: the
TypeScript one the refusal of `match`, and the Python one a study of
the five individuals that `i2` is not among.

refusals.match: `kinship` is .*, and the kinship a mixed model takes is a `Kinship`

refusals.case: the grammar gamma approximation with no kinship
refusals.match: a study with no kinship has no such denominator

refusals.match: GRAMMAR-Gamma approximation is being written
